# Manual routing

# Manual routes (React, Vue, any router)

Topic: `manual-routes` · Named Routes v2.2.0

When routes are declared in code (React Router <Route>, a vue-router routes array, Express-like servers), write the manifest yourself with createRoutes. You get the same name inference, parameter checking, encoding, query/hash, basePath and i18n options; only discovery is manual.

Patterns use the bracket syntax regardless of the router's own syntax: /users/:id becomes /users/[id], an optional :id? becomes [[id]], a splat * becomes [...splat] or [[...splat]]. Keep the object literal (or as const) so names and parameters are inferred.

With direct createRoutes(), includeBasePath defaults to false. For router links keep internal URLs; use route.url() for public URLs. Generator-based manual manifests include the configured base by default; set defaults.includeBasePath: false for a router that applies it itself.

## Without base path

The application is served at the domain root. Do not configure a navigation prefix.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";

const route = createRoutes({ home: "/", "users.show": "/users/[id]" });
route("users.show", { id: 42 }); // /users/42
route.url("users.show", { params: { id: 42 } }); // /users/42
```

## With base path

The application is served under /app. Configure the framework base before regenerating the routes.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";

const route = createRoutes({ home: "/", "users.show": "/users/[id]" }, { basePath: "/app" });
route("users.show", { id: 42 }); // /users/42
route.url("users.show", { params: { id: 42 } }); // /app/users/42
```

Related topic IDs: helper-create-routes, public-url, config-discovery, config-extra-routes, assets


# Build URLs & name routes

# route()

Topic: `helper-route` · Named Routes v2.2.0

route(name, params?, options?) returns a URL string for a known route; it does not navigate. Required path parameters are typed and validated. Query, hash and locale belong in the third argument. For a public URL or a named options object use route.url().

Use route() for native router navigation in Next.js, Nuxt, Vue Router, React Router and TanStack Router. Generated Astro, SvelteKit and manual manifests include a configured base by default. Use route.url() for a public URL in every framework. Explicit defaults.includeBasePath and per-call basePath override the default; absolute URLs always include the configured base.

## Without base path

The application is served at the domain root. Do not configure a navigation prefix.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const route = createRoutes({ home: "/", "users.show": "/users/[id]" });

route("home"); // /
route("users.show", { id: 42 }); // /users/42
```

## With base path

The application is served under /app. Configure the framework base before regenerating the routes.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const route = createRoutes({ home: "/", "users.show": "/users/[id]" }, { basePath: "/app", includeBasePath: true });

route("home"); // /app
route("users.show", { id: 42 }); // /app/users/42
route("users.show", { id: 42 }, { basePath: false }); // /users/42
```

Related topic IDs: public-url, parameters, query-hash, base-path
---

# route.url() — public URLs

Topic: `public-url` · Named Routes v2.2.0

Signature: route.url(name, { params?, query?, hash?, locale?, absolute?, basePath? }). The options object is optional only when the path and query schema allow it. The configured base is included by default; pass basePath: false for an internal path. The function returns string, so use route() for a native typed Link.

Use route() for native router navigation in Next.js, Nuxt, Vue Router, React Router and TanStack Router. Generated Astro, SvelteKit and manual manifests include a configured base by default. Use route.url() for a public URL in every framework. Explicit defaults.includeBasePath and per-call basePath override the default; absolute URLs always include the configured base.

## Without base path

The application is served at the domain root. Do not configure a navigation prefix.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const route = createRoutes({ entrar: "/entrar", "users.show": "/users/[id]" });

route.url("entrar"); // /entrar
route.url("users.show", { params: { id: 42 }, query: { tab: "posts" } });
// /users/42?tab=posts
```

## With base path

The application is served under /app. Configure the framework base before regenerating the routes.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const route = createRoutes({ entrar: "/entrar", "users.show": "/users/[id]" }, { basePath: "/app" });

route.url("entrar"); // /app/entrar
route.url("users.show", { params: { id: 42 }, query: { tab: "posts" } });
// /app/users/42?tab=posts
```

Related topic IDs: helper-route, base-path, helper-endpoint
---

# Required parameters & encoding

Topic: `parameters` · Named Routes v2.2.0

A [user] parameter accepts a nonempty string or finite number. Values are encoded as one URL segment: a slash inside a value is not a path separator. Missing, extra or invalid parameters are rejected. The helper validates URL construction, not resource existence.

```ts
route("users.$user", { user: "Ana Silva" }); // /users/Ana%20Silva
route("users.$user", { user: "a/b" }); // /users/a%2Fb
```

Related topic IDs: optional-parameters, catch-all-parameters, mixed-parameters, helper-route
---

# Optional route parameters

Topic: `optional-parameters` · Named Routes v2.2.0

Use [[id]] for an optional scalar. Omit the value to omit its segment. In a generated application, use the framework’s equivalent convention; support differs by router.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const route = createRoutes({ profile: "/users/[[id]]" });
route("profile"); // /users
route("profile", { id: 42 }); // /users/42
```

Related topic IDs: parameters, catch-all-parameters, naming
---

# Catch-all parameters

Topic: `catch-all-parameters` · Named Routes v2.2.0

A required [...slug] takes a nonempty array; optional [[...slug]] accepts omitted or empty values. Each element is encoded as a distinct segment. Do not pass a slash-separated string as a catch-all.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const route = createRoutes({ docs: "/docs/[[...slug]]" });
route("docs"); // /docs
route("docs", { slug: ["guide", "install"] }); // /docs/guide/install
```

Related topic IDs: optional-parameters, parameters
---

# Mixed route segments

Topic: `mixed-parameters` · Named Routes v2.2.0

A mixed segment combines literal text and required parameters. Every dynamic parameter still has its own typed key.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const route = createRoutes({ release: "/v[major]-[minor]" });
route("release", { major: 2, minor: 1 }); // /v2-1
```

Related topic IDs: parameters, naming
---

# Query strings

Topic: `query-hash` · Named Routes v2.2.0

Pass query in options to append key/value pairs. Numbers and booleans are serialized; arrays repeat the key; null and undefined are omitted. Query fields are distinct from path params. Typed schemas are optional.

```ts
route.url("products", { query: { page: 2, sort: "newest" } });
// /products?page=2&sort=newest
```

Related topic IDs: typed-query, helper-with-query, helper-parse-query, hash-fragments
---

# URL fragments (hash)

Topic: `hash-fragments` · Named Routes v2.2.0

Use hash to point to a section on a page. The helper removes an optional leading # and encodes the fragment. The browser does not send it to the server.

```ts
route.url("about", { hash: "team" }); // /about#team
```

Related topic IDs: query-hash, public-url
---

# Base path — internal vs public URL

Topic: `base-path` · Named Routes v2.2.0

Use route() for native router navigation in Next.js, Nuxt, Vue Router, React Router and TanStack Router. Generated Astro, SvelteKit and manual manifests include a configured base by default. Use route.url() for a public URL in every framework. Explicit defaults.includeBasePath and per-call basePath override the default; absolute URLs always include the configured base.

Use the framework-specific deployment guide to configure its router base. The CLI reuses the last successful framework base in .named-routes/ or accepts --base-path /app; --base-path / clears it. Do not treat an asset CDN as the navigation base.

## Without base path

The application is served at the domain root. Do not configure a navigation prefix.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const route = createRoutes({ about: "/about" });

route("about"); // /about
route.url("about"); // /about
```

## With base path

The application is served under /app. Configure the framework base before regenerating the routes.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const route = createRoutes({ about: "/about" }, { basePath: "/app" });

route("about"); // /about
route.url("about"); // /app/about
route.withDefaults({ includeBasePath: true })("about"); // /app/about
```

Related topic IDs: public-url, absolute-urls, trailing-slash, asset-base, cli-generate
---

# Absolute URLs & origin

Topic: `absolute-urls` · Named Routes v2.2.0

Set defaults.origin to a trusted HTTP(S) origin without credentials, path, query or hash. absolute: true includes the base. The runtime never guesses the origin from window or request headers; public config must not contain secrets.

## Without base path

The application is served at the domain root. Do not configure a navigation prefix.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const route = createRoutes({ about: "/about" }, { origin: "https://example.com" });
route.url("about", { absolute: true }); // https://example.com/about
```

## With base path

The application is served under /app. Configure the framework base before regenerating the routes.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const route = createRoutes({ about: "/about" }, { origin: "https://example.com", basePath: "/app" });
route.url("about", { absolute: true }); // https://example.com/app/about
```

Related topic IDs: base-path, helper-canonical, helper-with-defaults
---

# Trailing slashes

Topic: `trailing-slash` · Named Routes v2.2.0

trailingSlash changes generated path formatting, not server redirects. Configure the same policy in your framework. Next.js inherits this option from next.config.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const route = createRoutes({ about: "/about" }, { trailingSlash: true });
route("about"); // /about/
```

Related topic IDs: base-path, config-defaults
---

# Semantic route names and groups

Topic: `semantic-names` · Named Routes v2.2.0

Set naming.style to semantic to use index for parent pages and show for terminal required scalar parameters. Existing names remain the default. Static segment names are not translated or singularized. Set names to give individual URLs a stable semantic name (including create); update that map when the URL moves. Collisions fail generation rather than silently changing behavior.

```ts
// named-routes.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from "@triooo/named-routes/config";
export default defineConfig({
  naming: { style: "semantic" },
  names: { "/admin/alunos/novo": "admin.alunos.create" },
});
```

Related topic IDs: stable-names, naming, config-naming, generated-source
---

# Optional stable names

Topic: `stable-names` · Named Routes v2.2.0

Automatic names follow URL structure. If a refactor moves a public URL and you need a stable semantic name, update the optional names map. Every aliased path must exist. Unlisted routes keep automatic names. Duplicate names and typos fail generation instead of silently creating broken links.

A custom name replaces the automatic name for that path; it does not add a second alias automatically. This is useful for Laravel-style names such as posts.show, but it is not required for normal use.

```ts
export default {
  names: {
    "/posts": "posts.index",
    "/posts/[post]": "posts.show",
    "/posts/[post]/edit": "posts.edit",
  },
};
// After generation:
// route("posts.show", { post: 42 });
```

Related topic IDs: semantic-names, config-naming, naming
---

# TypeScript and Next typedRoutes

Topic: `typescript` · Named Routes v2.2.0

Literal patterns infer name unions and parameter objects. Required parameters are checked at compile time; optional catch-all routes can be called without parameters. The runtime still validates JavaScript callers.

Since 2.0 route() returns typed hrefs (see Typed hrefs): template literal types that Next.js typedRoutes, <Link> and router.push() accept without asserting Route. hrefs: "string" returns string as in 1.x. The exported types need TypeScript 5.4+. Do not assert untrusted arbitrary input to a route name to bypass validation.

```ts
import type { RouteName } from "@/routes.generated";
import { route } from "@/routes.generated";
const name: RouteName = "user.profile";
route("users.$user", { user: 42 });
// route("unknown");          // Type error
// route("users.$user");     // Missing user
// route("users.$user", { id: 42 }); // Wrong parameter
// With Next typedRoutes (typed hrefs are the default):
// <Link href={route(name)}>Profile</Link>   // no cast
```


# Route reference & inspection

# Reverse routing and active routes

Topic: `reverse-routing` · Named Routes v2.2.0

route.match(url) returns the named route a path points to, with decoded params, the query (repeated keys become arrays), the hash and the locale, or null. It accepts a root-relative path such as /users/42?tab=posts#bio or a URL object; absolute URLs match only on the configured origin or an i18n domain. route.is(name, url) compares a URL with a route; { exact: false } also accepts descendants, for active navigation sections. route.breadcrumbs(url) returns the matches of every ancestor path.

Static segments win, then mixed, dynamic, optional, catch-all and optional catch-all segments, compared from left to right; equally specific patterns resolve by declaration order. Segments are split before they are decoded, so %2F stays inside a parameter; malformed percent-encoding, empty segments and relative or protocol-relative URLs return null. Pass { basePath: true } when the URL includes basePath (window.location.pathname). Locale prefixes, custom prefixes and localized pathnames are recognized.

Matching describes your route table only: it is not authorization, does not prove a resource exists or that a navigation will succeed, and does not replace the framework router. The query is returned as strings; parse it with your own schema, for example schema.parse(found.query) with coercion.

```ts
const found = route.match("/users/42?tab=posts");
// { name: "users.$user", params: { user: "42" }, query: { tab: "posts" }, hash: "", locale: undefined, ... }
if (found?.name === "users.$user") found.params.user; // string

route.is("users.$user", "/users/new"); // false when /users/new is its own page
route.is("users", pathname, { exact: false }); // active section
route.breadcrumbs("/users/42/edit").map((item) => item.name);
// ["home", "users", "users.$user", "users.$user.edit"]
```

Related topic IDs: helper-match, helper-is, helper-breadcrumbs
---

# route.match()

Topic: `helper-match` · Named Routes v2.2.0

`route.match(url, options?)` recognizes a known path and returns a discriminated result with name, pattern, params, locale and raw query, or null. Use `{ basePath: true }` when the input includes the configured base. Parameters narrow by route name; use parseQuery for schema-based conversion. Matching is not authorization.

## Without base path

The application is served at the domain root. Do not configure a navigation prefix.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const route = createRoutes({ home: "/", users: "/users", "users.show": "/users/[id]" });

const found = route.match("/users/42?tab=posts");
if (found?.name === "users.show") console.log(found.params.id); // "42"
```

## With base path

The application is served under /app. Configure the framework base before regenerating the routes.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const route = createRoutes({ home: "/", users: "/users", "users.show": "/users/[id]" }, { basePath: "/app" });

const found = route.match("/app/users/42?tab=posts", { basePath: true });
if (found?.name === "users.show") console.log(found.params.id); // "42"
```

Related topic IDs: helper-is, helper-breadcrumbs, helper-parse-query
---

# route.is()

Topic: `helper-is` · Named Routes v2.2.0

`route.is(name, url, options?)` tests whether a URL matches the named route. Use `exact: false` to include matching descendants and `{ basePath: true }` for public URLs containing the base. This is useful for active navigation, not access control. Unknown route names are rejected.

## Without base path

The application is served at the domain root. Do not configure a navigation prefix.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const route = createRoutes({ home: "/", users: "/users", "users.show": "/users/[id]" });

route.is("users.show", "/users/42"); // true
route.is("users", "/users/42", { exact: false }); // true
```

## With base path

The application is served under /app. Configure the framework base before regenerating the routes.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const route = createRoutes({ home: "/", users: "/users", "users.show": "/users/[id]" }, { basePath: "/app" });

route.is("users.show", "/app/users/42", { basePath: true }); // true
route.is("users", "/app/users/42", { basePath: true, exact: false }); // true
```

Related topic IDs: helper-match, helper-breadcrumbs
---

# route.breadcrumbs()

Topic: `helper-breadcrumbs` · Named Routes v2.2.0

`route.breadcrumbs(url, options?)` returns known matches for ancestor paths, ordered from root to leaf. It does not invent missing routes or human-readable labels; map names to translated labels in your application. Supply `{ basePath: true }` for URLs containing the base.

## Without base path

The application is served at the domain root. Do not configure a navigation prefix.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const route = createRoutes({ home: "/", users: "/users", "users.show": "/users/[id]" });

route.breadcrumbs("/users/42").map((item) => item.name);
// ["home", "users", "users.show"]
```

## With base path

The application is served under /app. Configure the framework base before regenerating the routes.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const route = createRoutes({ home: "/", users: "/users", "users.show": "/users/[id]" }, { basePath: "/app" });

route.breadcrumbs("/app/users/42", { basePath: true }).map((item) => item.name);
// ["home", "users", "users.show"]
```

Related topic IDs: helper-match, helper-is
---

# route.has()

Topic: `helper-has` · Named Routes v2.2.0

`route.has(name)` checks the manifest and narrows an arbitrary string to a valid route name. It does not check whether a server currently serves the route. Use it before accessing routes selected from external input.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const urls = createRoutes({ home: "/", about: "/about" });
function patternFor(name: string) {
  return urls.has(name) ? urls.pattern(name) : null;
}
patternFor("about"); // /about
patternFor("missing"); // null
```

Related topic IDs: helper-names, helper-pattern
---

# route.names()

Topic: `helper-names` · Named Routes v2.2.0

`route.names()` returns the known names as a typed array. Use it for debugging or development tools; it does not expose authorization rules or guarantee that every route is reachable by a given user.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const urls = createRoutes({ home: "/", about: "/about" });
urls.names(); // ["home", "about"]
```

Related topic IDs: helper-has, helper-pattern
---

# route.pattern()

Topic: `helper-pattern` · Named Routes v2.2.0

`route.pattern(name, locale?)` returns the route template, not a generated URL. Passing a locale returns its localized template when configured. It does not substitute parameters or add a locale or base prefix. Use route() to create a navigable URL.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const urls = createRoutes({ about: "/about", "posts.show": "/posts/[id]" }, {
  i18n: {
    locales: ["en", "pt"], defaultLocale: "pt", localePrefix: "always",
    pathnames: { "/about": { pt: "/sobre" }, "/posts/[id]": { pt: "/artigos/[id]" } },
  },
});
urls.pattern("posts.show"); // /posts/[id]
urls.pattern("posts.show", "pt"); // /artigos/[id]
urls("posts.show", { id: 42 }, { locale: "pt" }); // /pt/artigos/42
```

Related topic IDs: helper-parse-pattern, helper-format-pattern
---

# createRoutes()

Topic: `helper-create-routes` · Named Routes v2.2.0

Create an independent, frozen helper from a name-to-pattern manifest. Keep literal types for autocomplete. Defaults apply to the returned helper; no filesystem or framework imports are required in the browser.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const route = createRoutes({ home: "/", "users.show": "/users/[id]" });
route("users.show", { id: 42 }); // /users/42
```

Related topic IDs: manual-routes, helper-route, helper-with-defaults
---

# route.withDefaults()

Topic: `helper-with-defaults` · Named Routes v2.2.0

Create an isolated helper with origin, basePath, assetBase or trailingSlash overrides. Routes, locale rules, bound locale, manifest and query schemas remain available. The original helper is unchanged; use a trusted tenant configuration on the server, not arbitrary Host headers. The returned helper conservatively types generated hrefs as string.

## Without base path

The application is served at the domain root. Do not configure a navigation prefix.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const route = createRoutes({ about: "/about" }, { origin: "https://example.com" });

const tenant = route.withDefaults({ origin: "https://tenant.example.com", assetBase: "https://cdn.tenant.example.com" });
tenant.canonical("about"); // https://tenant.example.com/about
tenant.asset("logo.svg"); // https://cdn.tenant.example.com/logo.svg
route.canonical("about"); // https://example.com/about
```

## With base path

The application is served under /app. Configure the framework base before regenerating the routes.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const route = createRoutes({ about: "/about" }, { origin: "https://example.com" });

const tenant = route.withDefaults({ origin: "https://tenant.example.com", basePath: "/dashboard", assetBase: "https://cdn.tenant.example.com" });
tenant.canonical("about"); // https://tenant.example.com/dashboard/about
tenant.asset("logo.svg"); // https://cdn.tenant.example.com/logo.svg
route.canonical("about"); // https://example.com/about
```

Related topic IDs: base-path, absolute-urls, helper-create-routes
---

# parsePattern()

Topic: `helper-parse-pattern` · Named Routes v2.2.0

Parse and validate a canonical pattern into segment records. Use it in tooling, not instead of route() for navigation.

```ts
import { parsePattern } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const segments = parsePattern("/users/[id]");
console.log(segments.map((segment) => segment.kind)); // ["static", "dynamic"]
```

Related topic IDs: helper-create-routes, parameters, helper-pattern
---

# formatPattern()

Topic: `helper-format-pattern` · Named Routes v2.2.0

Serialize segment records back into the canonical bracket syntax. This is a pattern, not a concrete URL.

```ts
import { formatPattern, parsePattern } from "@triooo/named-routes";
formatPattern(parsePattern("/users/[id]")); // /users/[id]
```

Related topic IDs: helper-create-routes, parameters, helper-pattern
---

# patternParameters()

Topic: `helper-pattern-parameters` · Named Routes v2.2.0

List parameter names from parsed segments. This is useful when inspecting a manifest or generating tooling.

```ts
import { parsePattern, patternParameters } from "@triooo/named-routes";
patternParameters(parsePattern("/users/[id]")); // ["id"]
```

Related topic IDs: helper-create-routes, parameters, helper-pattern


# Typed queries & URL updates

# Typed query parameters

Topic: `typed-query` · Named Routes v2.2.0

Declare per-route query schemas in a module whose default export is defineQuery({...}) and point the query option to it. Keys are route names; values are Standard Schema validators (Zod 3.24+, Valibot 1+, ArkType and others) or defineQuery.type<T>() for TypeScript-only types. Routes without a schema keep the 1.0 query.

With a schema, TypeScript rejects unknown keys and incompatible values, and required keys make options.query required. No schema library becomes a dependency: TypeScript outputs import the module as types only, so nothing is bundled and nothing is validated at runtime.

Set validateQuery: true to bundle the schemas and validate every query object when a URL is built; failures throw INVALID_QUERY with the issues. Validation never changes the URL: values are serialized as you pass them, without the schema's defaults or transforms. Asynchronous schemas are rejected because route() is synchronous. JavaScript outputs import the module as a value to infer its types. Zod 4 and Valibot 1 require TypeScript 5.4+.

route.parseQuery(name, url) reads a URL's query back with the route's schema when it is available at runtime (validateQuery: true, or schemas passed to createRoutes) and returns { ok: true, value } with the schema's output type, or { ok: false, issues }. Values arrive as strings; for keys the schema rejects, the strings route() writes for numbers and true/false are converted back and a single value becomes an array, so one schema both builds and parses. Routes without a runtime schema (no schema, defineQuery.type() or schemas imported as types only) return the raw query, and their type says so.

```ts
// src/route-query.ts
import { defineQuery } from "@triooo/named-routes";
import { z } from "zod";

export default defineQuery({
  products: z.object({
    page: z.number().int().min(1).optional(),
    sort: z.enum(["newest", "price"]).optional(),
  }),
  search: defineQuery.type<{ q: string }>(),
});
```

Related topic IDs: query-schema-config, query-schema-use, helper-parse-query, helper-define-query
---

# Connect a query schema

Topic: `query-schema-config` · Named Routes v2.2.0

Point query at the module with the default defineQuery export. Enable validateQuery only when you want the runtime validator bundled; type-only schemas never validate values at runtime.

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "@triooo/named-routes/config";
export default defineConfig({ query: "src/route-query.ts", validateQuery: true });
```

Related topic IDs: typed-query, query-schema-use, helper-parse-query
---

# Use typed queries

Topic: `query-schema-use` · Named Routes v2.2.0

After configuring the products and search schemas in the typed query guide, regenerate the module. TypeScript rejects unknown keys and requires mandatory query parameters.

```ts
route("products", {}, { query: { page: 2, sort: "newest" } }); // /products?page=2&sort=newest
route("products", {}, { query: { pgae: 2 } }); // type error: unknown key
route("search"); // type error: q is required
```

Related topic IDs: typed-query, query-schema-config, helper-parse-query
---

# defineQuery()

Topic: `helper-define-query` · Named Routes v2.2.0

Use a per-route Standard Schema map. The helper preserves input and output types. A synchronous validator can be used for runtime validation; the schema package is your optional dependency.

```ts
import { defineQuery } from "@triooo/named-routes";
import { z } from "zod";

export default defineQuery({ products: z.object({ page: z.number().int().min(1) }) });
```

Related topic IDs: typed-query, query-schema-config, helper-parse-query
---

# defineQuery.type<T>()

Topic: `helper-define-query-type` · Named Routes v2.2.0

Declare a query contract using TypeScript only. It adds no runtime validator. Do not trust user-provided URL values without validating them separately.

```ts
import { defineQuery } from "@triooo/named-routes";
export default defineQuery({ search: defineQuery.type<{ q: string }>() });
```

Related topic IDs: helper-define-query, typed-query, helper-parse-query
---

# route.parseQuery()

Topic: `helper-parse-query` · Named Routes v2.2.0

`route.parseQuery(name, input)` reads query parameters from a URL or query string and returns a result with `ok`. A runtime Standard Schema converts and validates values; type-only schemas return raw values instead. In generated modules use `query` and `validateQuery: true` to include schemas at runtime. Zod below is an optional consumer dependency. Do not assume a failed result contains a valid value.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
import { defineQuery } from "@triooo/named-routes";
import { z } from "zod";
const urls = createRoutes({ products: "/products" }, {}, {
  query: defineQuery({ products: z.object({ page: z.number().int().min(1) }) }),
});
const parsed = urls.parseQuery("products", "?page=2");
if (parsed.ok) {
  console.log(parsed.value.page); // 2 (number)
}
urls.parseQuery("products", "?page=0").ok; // false
```
---

# route.withQuery()

Topic: `helper-with-query` · Named Routes v2.2.0

Update a root-relative or HTTP(S) URL without recreating its path or hash. Set null or [] to remove a key, undefined to preserve it, and an array to replace repeated values. Unchanged repeated values remain. Query encoding is normalized by URLSearchParams. Pass { name, basePath: true } when validating a known prefixed route; named patches use the route query input type. When a runtime schema is available for the matched route, the complete resulting query is validated. Type-only schemas do not validate at runtime.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const urls = createRoutes({ products: "/products" });
urls.withQuery("/products?page=1&category=books#list", { page: 2 });
// /products?category=books&page=2#list
urls.withQuery("/products?page=2&category=books", { category: null });
// /products?page=2
urls.withQuery("/products?tag=a&tag=b", { tag: ["c", "d"] });
// /products?tag=c&tag=d
```


# Internationalization

# Locales and i18n

Topic: `i18n` · Named Routes v2.2.0

Configure i18n with locales, defaultLocale and optionally localePrefix, pathnames and domains. The shape matches next-intl's defineRouting(), so you can pass that routing object directly; next-intl-only keys such as localeCookie are accepted and ignored. In Next.js Pages Router projects, withNamedRoutes inherits next.config i18n automatically (localePrefix as-needed, domains included).

A dynamic first folder named locale or lang (app/[locale]/…, pages/[lang]/…, change it with localeParam) is removed from names and patterns: app/[locale]/about/page.tsx becomes about → /about. Physical locale folders (src/pages/pt/about.astro) merge into the same route. Without a locale folder (Pages Router i18n, @nuxtjs/i18n, middleware rewrites), every page is localized. Endpoints and routes outside [locale] are listed as unlocalized and never get a prefix.

route(name, params) without a locale returns the internal path, which is what next-intl's Link, Pages Router Link and @nuxtjs/i18n's localePath expect. Pass { locale } for plain anchors, redirects, sitemaps, emails or language switchers. route.forLocale(locale) returns a helper bound to that locale, and route.locales() lists the configured locales.

localePrefix: always (default) prefixes every locale; as-needed omits the default locale; never omits all prefixes; { mode, prefixes: { "en-US": "/us" } } customizes them. pathnames maps an internal pattern to localized patterns with the same parameters. With absolute: true, a locale served by a configured domain uses that domain as the origin. Locales are typed: the generated module exports RouteLocale and unknown locales are type and runtime errors.

**Translate incoming URLs.** route.localize('/sobre', 'en') returns /en/about when /sobre is the Portuguese pathname of /about and localePrefix is always. route.localize('/pt/produtos/42?tab=info#details', 'en') can return /en/products/42?tab=info#details. The method searches all configured languages, preserves path parameters and the original query/fragment, and returns null for unknown, ambiguous or unlocalized routes. Existing route.match() behavior does not change. A recognized source prefix, or sourceLocale for unprefixed aliases, disambiguates equally specific patterns. With no target locale, forLocale() supplies the bound locale, otherwise the configured default is used.

**Redirecting requests.** The runtime does not intercept requests. Resolve the preferred locale with your existing i18n middleware, call route.localize(pathAndQuery, locale, { basePath: true }) for a browser URL containing the base, and issue a temporary redirect only when the returned path differs. Let the existing framework handle its internal rewrites. For a raw internal path use includeBasePath: true to include the prefix in the result without requiring it in the input. For domain-based locale routing use absolute: true with configured domains and compare the entire URL. Do not redirect API/assets, non-GET/HEAD requests or an unresolved path. A ready Next.js proxy recipe is in examples/app-router/recipes/localized-redirect.ts.example.

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "@triooo/named-routes/config";
export default defineConfig({
  i18n: {
    locales: ["en", "pt"],
    defaultLocale: "en",
    localePrefix: "always",
    pathnames: { "/about": { en: "/about", pt: "/sobre" } },
  },
});
```

Related topic IDs: localized-url, helper-localize, helper-for-locale, helper-locales, helper-alternates
---

# Generate a localized URL

Topic: `localized-url` · Named Routes v2.2.0

With i18n configured as in the setup guide, locale selects the localized pathname and prefix. Keep native locale-aware links internal when they add locale themselves. The helper does not translate a dynamic slug value.

```ts
route.url("about", { locale: "pt" }); // /pt/sobre (always prefix, no base)
```

Related topic IDs: i18n, helper-localize, helper-for-locale
---

# route.localize()

Topic: `helper-localize` · Named Routes v2.2.0

`route.localize(url, locale?, options?)` translates an existing URL through the route table, preserving its query and fragment. Use it in language switchers and redirects. It returns null if no unambiguous localized route exists. For a public URL containing basePath, pass `{ basePath: true }`; use `sourceLocale` to disambiguate unprefixed translated paths when needed. It does not translate dynamic slug values or determine the visitor’s language.

## Without base path

The application is served at the domain root. Do not configure a navigation prefix.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const route = createRoutes({ about: "/about" }, { i18n: { locales: ["en", "pt"], defaultLocale: "en", localePrefix: "always", pathnames: { "/about": { pt: "/sobre" } } } });

route.localize("/pt/sobre?tab=info#top", "en");
// /en/about?tab=info#top
```

## With base path

The application is served under /app. Configure the framework base before regenerating the routes.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const route = createRoutes({ about: "/about" }, { basePath: "/app", i18n: { locales: ["en", "pt"], defaultLocale: "en", localePrefix: "always", pathnames: { "/about": { pt: "/sobre" } } } });

route.localize("/app/pt/sobre?tab=info#top", "en", { basePath: true });
// /app/en/about?tab=info#top
```
---

# route.locales()

Topic: `helper-locales` · Named Routes v2.2.0

`route.locales()` lists configured locales, or an empty array when i18n is absent. This is configuration, not browser or request language detection. Use it to populate a language selector.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const urls = createRoutes({ about: "/about", "posts.show": "/posts/[id]" }, {
  i18n: {
    locales: ["en", "pt"], defaultLocale: "pt", localePrefix: "always",
    pathnames: { "/about": { pt: "/sobre" }, "/posts/[id]": { pt: "/artigos/[id]" } },
  },
});
urls.locales(); // ["en", "pt"]
createRoutes({ home: "/" }).locales(); // []
```
---

# route.forLocale()

Topic: `helper-for-locale` · Named Routes v2.2.0

`route.forLocale(locale)` creates a helper bound to a configured locale. An explicit locale option on a later call can override it. The original helper is unchanged and assets never inherit the locale. Use this for a set of links in a known language.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const urls = createRoutes({ about: "/about", "posts.show": "/posts/[id]" }, {
  i18n: {
    locales: ["en", "pt"], defaultLocale: "pt", localePrefix: "always",
    pathnames: { "/about": { pt: "/sobre" }, "/posts/[id]": { pt: "/artigos/[id]" } },
  },
});
const pt = urls.forLocale("pt");
pt("about"); // /pt/sobre
pt("posts.show", { id: 42 }); // /pt/artigos/42
urls("about"); // /about
pt.asset("logo.svg"); // /logo.svg
```


# Assets & CDN

# asset() / route.asset()

Topic: `assets` · Named Routes v2.2.0

Use `asset(path, { absolute?: boolean })` or `route.asset()` for public URLs in any supported framework. Unlike named routes, public asset URLs include the effective `basePath` by default. They are unaffected by locale, trailingSlash, route names and query schemas. The helper builds URLs only; it does not check the filesystem, upload files, configure the CDN or replace imported assets, image optimization or bundler hashing.

Put files in `public/` for Next.js, Nuxt, Astro and the usual Vite apps; SvelteKit uses `static/` by default. Supply the file path relative to that directory (with or without one initial slash), not the directory name or an already prefixed path. For example `asset("images/logo.svg")` includes `/app` once when the base is `/app`. Unicode and spaces are URL-encoded; query strings and fragments are preserved. Do not pass untrusted URL input without application-level validation.

Set `defaults.assetBase` in named-routes.config to override the route base for assets: `"/files"`, `"/"` (root), or `"https://cdn.example.com/public"`. The default is the effective `basePath` from Next, Nuxt or Astro, or the router base configured for Vite and manual manifests. If Vite base, Nuxt CDN URL, or Next assetPrefix differs from that path, configure assetBase explicitly: bundler-specific prefixes are not inferred. Deploy the public files at that URL yourself. `absolute: true` requires defaults.origin unless the URL or assetBase is already absolute; it never uses the request host or locale domain. Valid HTTP(S) URLs passed directly are unchanged; protocol-relative URLs, non-HTTP schemes, credentials, ambiguous paths and traversal segments are rejected.

The generated module exports `asset` alongside `route` and `routes`. A manual manifest exposes `route.asset`. See the separate assetBase & CDN guide for hosting files outside the navigation base.

**Typed assets.** Enable assets: { strict: true } in named-routes.config; public paths are inferred from the local public directory (static/ in SvelteKit). See Typed assets, Asset versioning and Audit.

## Without base path

Public file URL: `/images/logo.svg`.

```ts
import { asset } from "@/routes.generated";

asset("images/logo.svg"); // /images/logo.svg
```

## With base path

Public file URL: `/app/images/logo.svg`.

```ts
import { asset } from "@/routes.generated";

asset("images/logo.svg"); // /app/images/logo.svg
```

Related topic IDs: asset-base, asset-absolute, typed-assets, asset-has, asset-versioning
---

# route.asset()

Topic: `helper-route-asset` · Named Routes v2.2.0

The bound asset helper is exposed as route.asset on every runtime helper, including typed helpers. A generated module normally also exports asset directly; both share the same defaults and manifest.

## Without base path

The application is served at the domain root. Do not configure a navigation prefix.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const route = createRoutes({ home: "/" });
route.asset("logo.svg"); // /logo.svg
```

## With base path

The application is served under /app. Configure the framework base before regenerating the routes.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const route = createRoutes({ home: "/" }, { basePath: "/app" });
route.asset("logo.svg"); // /app/logo.svg
```

Related topic IDs: assets, asset-base
---

# assetBase & CDN

Topic: `asset-base` · Named Routes v2.2.0

`defaults.assetBase` overrides the public file prefix independently of `basePath`. Use an HTTP(S) CDN URL, a root-relative prefix, or `/` to opt out of the navigation base. It does not deploy files or configure a CDN. Keep secrets out of defaults; they are serialized to the generated module. In named-routes.config use the same defaults object.

## Without base path

Public file URL: `https://cdn.example.com/public/logo.svg`.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const route = createRoutes({ about: "/about" }, { assetBase: "https://cdn.example.com/public" });

route.asset("logo.svg"); // https://cdn.example.com/public/logo.svg
route.url("about"); // /about
```

## With base path

Public file URL: `https://cdn.example.com/public/logo.svg`.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const route = createRoutes({ about: "/about" }, { basePath: "/app", assetBase: "https://cdn.example.com/public" });

route.asset("logo.svg"); // https://cdn.example.com/public/logo.svg
route.url("about"); // /app/about
const rootAssets = route.withDefaults({ assetBase: "/" });
rootAssets.asset("logo.svg"); // /logo.svg
```
---

# Absolute asset URLs

Topic: `asset-absolute` · Named Routes v2.2.0

Pass absolute: true to combine the trusted origin with the asset path. If assetBase is an absolute CDN URL, it is already absolute. Locale does not affect asset URLs.

## Without base path

The application is served at the domain root. Do not configure a navigation prefix.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const { asset } = createRoutes({ home: "/" }, { origin: "https://example.com" });
asset("images/logo.svg", { absolute: true }); // https://example.com/images/logo.svg
```

## With base path

The application is served under /app. Configure the framework base before regenerating the routes.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const { asset } = createRoutes({ home: "/" }, { basePath: "/app", origin: "https://example.com" });
asset("images/logo.svg", { absolute: true }); // https://example.com/app/images/logo.svg
```

Related topic IDs: assets, asset-base, absolute-urls
---

# Typed assets

Topic: `typed-assets` · Named Routes v2.2.0

Enable `assets` in named-routes.config. The generator scans public/ (static/ in SvelteKit), ignores hidden files and symlinks, supports *, ** and ? exclude globs, and writes an encoded relative path manifest with SHA-256 hashes. Set strict: true for literal path checking on the generated asset export; route.asset() checks the manifest at runtime. Remote HTTP(S) URLs remain allowed. No files are uploaded. Change assets.directory for a custom public directory. Build/check regenerate the manifest; the CLI watch watches it recursively.

```ts
// named-routes.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from "@triooo/named-routes/config";
export default defineConfig({
  assets: { enabled: true, strict: true, exclude: ["**/*.map"] },
  defaults: { basePath: "/app", assetBase: "https://cdn.example.com/public" },
});
```
---

# asset.has() / paths() / info()

Topic: `asset-metadata` · Named Routes v2.2.0

Inspect the generated manifest, not the deployed server. has accepts a local path with an optional leading slash/query/hash; paths returns encoded names; info returns path, extension, size in bytes and version, or null. Without asset discovery these methods report an empty manifest.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const { asset } = createRoutes({ home: "/" }, {
  assetManifest: { files: { "images/logo.svg": { size: 64, version: "a8f32c910123" } } },
});
asset.has("images/logo.svg"); // true
asset.paths(); // ["images/logo.svg"]
asset.info("images/logo.svg"); // { path, extension, size, version }
asset.info("missing.svg"); // null
```

Related topic IDs: asset-has, asset-paths, asset-info, typed-assets
---

# asset.has()

Topic: `asset-has` · Named Routes v2.2.0

Check whether a local path is in the generated asset manifest. This is not a network request and does not verify deployment.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const { asset } = createRoutes({ home: "/" }, {
  assetManifest: { files: { "images/logo.svg": { size: 64, version: "a8f32c910123" } } },
});
asset.has("images/logo.svg"); // true
asset.has("missing.svg"); // false
```

Related topic IDs: typed-assets, assets, asset-versioning
---

# asset.paths()

Topic: `asset-paths` · Named Routes v2.2.0

List encoded public paths from the asset manifest. An unconfigured manifest returns an empty list.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const { asset } = createRoutes({ home: "/" }, {
  assetManifest: { files: { "images/logo.svg": { size: 64, version: "a8f32c910123" } } },
});
asset.paths(); // ["images/logo.svg"]
```

Related topic IDs: typed-assets, assets, asset-versioning
---

# asset.info()

Topic: `asset-info` · Named Routes v2.2.0

Read metadata (path, extension, size and version) for a known public file; unknown paths return null.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const { asset } = createRoutes({ home: "/" }, {
  assetManifest: { files: { "images/logo.svg": { size: 64, version: "a8f32c910123" } } },
});
const logo = asset.info("images/logo.svg");
console.log(logo?.size); // 64
asset.info("missing.svg"); // null
```

Related topic IDs: typed-assets, assets, asset-versioning
---

# Asset versioning

Topic: `asset-versioning` · Named Routes v2.2.0

Use `{ version: true }` to append or replace v with the first 12 hexadecimal digits of the SHA-256 content hash. Existing query values and fragments remain. Enable asset discovery, then rebuild when content changes. Remote URLs and missing entries cannot be versioned. This is cache busting, not a cryptographic integrity guarantee or a CDN purge.

## Without base path

The application is served at the domain root. Do not configure a navigation prefix.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const { asset } = createRoutes({ home: "/" }, {
  assetManifest: { files: { "css/custom.css": { size: 64, version: "a8f32c910123" } } },
});
asset("css/custom.css", { version: true });
// /css/custom.css?v=a8f32c910123
asset("css/custom.css?theme=dark#top", { version: true });
// /css/custom.css?theme=dark&v=a8f32c910123#top
```

## With base path

The application is served under /app. Configure the framework base before regenerating the routes.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const { asset } = createRoutes({ home: "/" }, {
  basePath: "/app",
  assetManifest: { files: { "css/custom.css": { size: 64, version: "a8f32c910123" } } },
});
asset("css/custom.css", { version: true });
// /app/css/custom.css?v=a8f32c910123
asset("css/custom.css?theme=dark#top", { version: true });
// /app/css/custom.css?theme=dark&v=a8f32c910123#top
```


# SEO & metadata

# route.canonical()

Topic: `helper-canonical` · Named Routes v2.2.0

Generate an absolute URL for metadata, using the explicit, bound or default locale (if configured). Canonical URLs always include the navigation base. Query and hash are included only if explicitly provided. It does not decide which content is canonical or remove tracking parameters automatically.

## Without base path

The application is served at the domain root. Do not configure a navigation prefix.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const route = createRoutes({ about: "/about" }, { origin: "https://example.com", i18n: { locales: ["en", "pt"], defaultLocale: "en", localePrefix: "always", pathnames: { "/about": { pt: "/sobre" } } } });

route.canonical("about", {}, { locale: "pt" });
// https://example.com/pt/sobre
```

## With base path

The application is served under /app. Configure the framework base before regenerating the routes.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const route = createRoutes({ about: "/about" }, { basePath: "/app", origin: "https://example.com", i18n: { locales: ["en", "pt"], defaultLocale: "en", localePrefix: "always", pathnames: { "/about": { pt: "/sobre" } } } });

route.canonical("about", {}, { locale: "pt" });
// https://example.com/app/pt/sobre
```
---

# route.alternates()

Topic: `helper-alternates` · Named Routes v2.2.0

Build a map of locale URLs using existing pathnames, domains, params and query options. Absolute by default, with the base included. For nonlocalized routes or no i18n, returns an empty map. Use for hreflang and multilingual sitemaps; provide actual dynamic parameters. Locale slugs are not automatically translated.

## Without base path

The application is served at the domain root. Do not configure a navigation prefix.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const route = createRoutes({ about: "/about" }, { origin: "https://example.com", i18n: { locales: ["en", "pt"], defaultLocale: "en", localePrefix: "always", pathnames: { "/about": { pt: "/sobre" } } } });

route.alternates("about");
// { en: "https://example.com/en/about", pt: "https://example.com/pt/sobre" }
```

## With base path

The application is served under /app. Configure the framework base before regenerating the routes.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const route = createRoutes({ about: "/about" }, { basePath: "/app", origin: "https://example.com", i18n: { locales: ["en", "pt"], defaultLocale: "en", localePrefix: "always", pathnames: { "/about": { pt: "/sobre" } } } });

route.alternates("about");
// { en: "https://example.com/app/en/about", pt: "https://example.com/app/pt/sobre" }
```


# HTTP endpoints

# Generated api — HTTP descriptors

Topic: `endpoint-methods` · Named Routes v2.2.0

Enable includeApi: true. The generated api export contains only statically declared method names. Next App Router, SvelteKit and Astro use explicit named exports; Nuxt uses method suffixes. Next Pages API, generic handlers, Vue client routes, React Router actions/loaders and TanStack client routes cannot reliably declare HTTP methods this way. Unknown methods are not guessed. api.admin.post() returns {method, url}; it does not perform a request. Nested route names are flat keys such as api["admin.alunos"].get().

## Without base path

Browser URL: `/api/admin`.

```ts
// app/api/admin/route.ts exports GET and POST; includeApi: true
// In a separate consumer module:
import { api } from "@/routes.generated";

const { method, url } = api.admin.post();
await fetch(url, { method, body: JSON.stringify({ name: "Ana" }),
  headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" } });
```

## With base path

Browser URL: `/app/api/admin`.

```ts
// app/api/admin/route.ts exports GET and POST; includeApi: true
// In a separate consumer module:
import { api } from "@/routes.generated";

const { method, url } = api.admin.post();
await fetch(url, { method, body: JSON.stringify({ name: "Ana" }),
  headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" } });
```

Related topic IDs: config-api, helper-endpoint, endpoint-dynamic, nextjs-endpoints, nuxt-endpoints, sveltekit-endpoints, astro-endpoints
---

# route.endpoint()

Topic: `helper-endpoint` · Named Routes v2.2.0

Bind an explicit HTTP method to a known route. Calling the returned function produces a readonly descriptor with method and URL; it does not validate server capabilities or execute a request. Prefer generated api descriptors when discovery knows the methods.

## Without base path

The application is served at the domain root. Do not configure a navigation prefix.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const route = createRoutes({ "api.users": "/api/users/[id]" });
const updateUser = route.endpoint("api.users", "PATCH");
updateUser({ params: { id: 42 } }); // { method: "PATCH", url: "/api/users/42" }
```

## With base path

The application is served under /app. Configure the framework base before regenerating the routes.

```ts
import { createRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes";
const route = createRoutes({ "api.users": "/api/users/[id]" }, { basePath: "/app" });
const updateUser = route.endpoint("api.users", "PATCH");
updateUser({ params: { id: 42 } }); // { method: "PATCH", url: "/app/api/users/42" }
```

Related topic IDs: endpoint-methods, public-url
---

# Dynamic endpoint parameters

Topic: `endpoint-dynamic` · Named Routes v2.2.0

Generated api keys are flat names without a leading api. A key with dots or special characters uses brackets. In path naming mode /api/admin/alunos/[aluno] becomes api.admin.alunos.$aluno in the route manifest and admin.alunos.$aluno in the api export.

## Without base path

Browser URL: `/api/admin/alunos/42`.

```ts
import { api } from "@/routes.generated";
const { method, url } = api["admin.alunos.$aluno"].get({ params: { aluno: 42 } });
```

## With base path

Browser URL: `/app/api/admin/alunos/42`.

```ts
import { api } from "@/routes.generated";
const { method, url } = api["admin.alunos.$aluno"].get({ params: { aluno: 42 } });
```

Related topic IDs: endpoint-methods, helper-endpoint, semantic-names


# Configuration & runtime reference

# Runtime API reference

Topic: `runtime-api` · Named Routes v2.2.0

createRoutes(manifest, defaults?) creates an independent frozen helper and snapshots the manifest. Defaults contains basePath, assetBase, trailingSlash, origin and i18n. parsePattern(pattern) returns static/dynamic/optionalDynamic/catchAll/optional/mixed segment records and validates route syntax; formatPattern is its inverse and patternParameters lists parameter names. RouteValue, QueryValue, RouteParams, RouteOptions, RouteDefaults, I18nOptions, LocalePrefix, LocaleDomain, NamedRoutes and PatternSegment are exported types.

A manifest typed as a plain Record<string, string> (for example loaded from JSON) still works: names become string and parameters become a loose record, while the runtime keeps validating every call.

Related topic IDs: helper-route, public-url, helper-create-routes, helper-endpoint, helper-match, helper-parse-pattern, helper-define-query, assets
---

# Generator configuration

Topic: `configuration` · Named Routes v2.2.0

A configuration file is optional. The integrations generate routes with defaults; add only the settings you need. Files are discovered in .ts, .mts, .mjs, .js, .cjs, .json order; use .mjs if Node cannot load TypeScript configs. defineConfig gives autocomplete and rejects unknown options during generation. The CLI --config selects another file.

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "@triooo/named-routes/config";
export default defineConfig({});
```

Related topic IDs: config-discovery, config-output, config-naming, config-defaults, config-api, config-extra-routes
---

# Discovery & directories

Topic: `config-discovery` · Named Routes v2.2.0

Use framework: auto (default) or an explicit framework. discovery: framework reads a published table where supported; files forces the convention scanner. Next has router, appDir and pagesDir; other frameworks use routesDir. pageExtensions and exclude customize scanning. root is relative to the config file when configured there.

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "@triooo/named-routes/config";
export default defineConfig({
  framework: "next",
  router: "app",
  appDir: "src/app",
  exclude: ["**/__tests__/**"],
});
```

Related topic IDs: discovery, architecture, naming
---

# Generated output & exports

Topic: `config-output` · Named Routes v2.2.0

output defaults to src/routes.generated.ts; use .ts, .mts, .js or .mjs outside a routable directory. exportNames renames generated exports; importSource changes the runtime import specifier. hrefs: typed is the default; string restores plain string return types.

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "@triooo/named-routes/config";
export default defineConfig({
  output: "src/lib/routes.generated.ts",
  hrefs: "typed",
});
```

Related topic IDs: generated-source, typed-hrefs
---

# Naming conventions

Topic: `config-naming` · Named Routes v2.2.0

naming.style controls path or semantic names. separator, paramPrefix and home customize the path convention; transform can override an automatic name in a JavaScript or TypeScript config. names wins over automatic naming. Collisions fail generation.

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "@triooo/named-routes/config";
export default defineConfig({
  naming: { style: "semantic" },
  names: { "/admin/alunos/novo": "admin.alunos.create" },
});
```

Related topic IDs: semantic-names, stable-names, naming
---

# URL defaults

Topic: `config-defaults` · Named Routes v2.2.0

defaults contains basePath, includeBasePath, origin, trailingSlash and assetBase. These are public values serialized into the generated module. Explicit base settings override inherited framework values. Use a trusted origin, never credentials.

## Without base path

The application is served at the domain root. Do not configure a navigation prefix.

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "@triooo/named-routes/config";
export default defineConfig({
  defaults: { origin: "https://example.com" },
});
```

## With base path

The application is served under /app. Configure the framework base before regenerating the routes.

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "@triooo/named-routes/config";
export default defineConfig({
  defaults: { basePath: "/app", origin: "https://example.com" },
});
```

Related topic IDs: base-path, asset-base, absolute-urls
---

# Add explicit routes

Topic: `config-extra-routes` · Named Routes v2.2.0

extraRoutes maps a chosen name to a canonical pattern for a rewrite destination, manual manifest or external route known to your application. Unlike names, the URL need not be discovered. The package does not create a page or server route.

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "@triooo/named-routes/config";
export default defineConfig({
  extraRoutes: { "public.login": "/login" },
});
```

Related topic IDs: stable-names, manual-routes, boundaries
---

# Enable API discovery

Topic: `config-api` · Named Routes v2.2.0

includeApi is false by default. Enable it to include endpoint URLs recognized by the adapter. Method descriptors are generated only where method declarations are statically identifiable. This is not OpenAPI generation or an authorization layer.

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "@triooo/named-routes/config";
export default defineConfig({
  includeApi: true,
});
```

Related topic IDs: endpoint-methods, helper-endpoint
---

# Watch & development options

Topic: `config-watch` · Named Routes v2.2.0

The integration handles updates during development. withNamedRoutes accepts watch, watchMode and watchInterval; use polling only when native events are unreliable. CLI watch supports --watch-mode poll. Restart the framework after changing its router base.

```ts
import { withNamedRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes/next";
export default withNamedRoutes({}, { watchMode: "poll", watchInterval: 750 });
```

Related topic IDs: development, cli-watch


# Generator & tooling API

# Programmatic generator API

Topic: `generator-api` · Named Routes v2.2.0

discoverRoutes(options?) returns root, framework, directories, routes, entries and the runtime defaults without writing. Each entry has name, path, file, router, framework and optionally variant and localized. Explicit extra routes have file: null and router: explicit.

generateRoutes(options?, { check?: boolean }?) additionally returns output and changed. check mode rejects stale output without modifying it. validateOptions(options) throws INVALID_CONFIG for unknown keys. Import /generator and /config only in Node tooling, never in client code. withNamedRoutes comes from /next and namedRoutes from /vite.

Related topic IDs: generator-discover, generator-generate, generator-validate, configuration
---

# discoverRoutes()

Topic: `generator-discover` · Named Routes v2.2.0

Node tooling only: discover route entries without writing the output file. Inspect entries, framework and discovery metadata.

```ts
import { discoverRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes/generator";
const result = await discoverRoutes({ root: ".", framework: "next" });
console.log(result.entries);
```

Related topic IDs: generator-api, discovery
---

# generateRoutes()

Topic: `generator-generate` · Named Routes v2.2.0

Node tooling only: discover and write the generated module. With check: true, reject a stale output without modifying it. Returns output and changed as well as discovery information.

```ts
import { generateRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes/generator";
const result = await generateRoutes({ root: "." });
console.log(result.output, result.changed);
await generateRoutes({ root: "." }, { check: true });
```

Related topic IDs: generator-api, cli-generate, cli-check
---

# validateOptions()

Topic: `generator-validate` · Named Routes v2.2.0

Validate generator options in Node tooling. Unknown keys or invalid values throw INVALID_CONFIG. defineConfig is the typed config authoring helper; actual generation validates the runtime input.

```ts
import { validateOptions } from "@triooo/named-routes/generator";
const options = validateOptions({ framework: "next", includeApi: true });
console.log(options.framework);
```

Related topic IDs: configuration, generator-api


# CLI, CI & troubleshooting

# CLI and CI

Topic: `cli` · Named Routes v2.2.0

The binary is named-routes. generate (default) writes the manifest. list prints discovered entries as JSON. check compares without writing and exits with code 1 when stale. watch generates initially and keeps the module current until SIGINT/SIGTERM (file events with a rescan, or polling with --watch-mode poll). init writes named-routes.config.mjs for the detected framework and never overwrites an existing config. doctor diagnoses the project without writing (see Diagnostics).

Flags: --root <directory>, --config <file>, --framework <name>, --output <file>, --routes-dir <dir>, --router <auto|app|pages>, --api, --watch-interval <ms>, --watch-mode <auto|native|poll>, --json, --strict, --no-color and --v2 (doctor), --to and --write (migrate), --version (-v), --help (-h). Run commands from the consumer with the local package installed. Errors print their code and, when known, the file, route, option and a fix.

If you commit the generated file, run check before the build. The integrations regenerate at build time, so a check run after that build cannot detect a previously stale committed file. Generation is deterministic, atomic and timestamp-free. Existing files without the generator signature are never overwritten.

migrate --to 2 prepares a 1.x project for 2.0: it pins hrefs: "string" and, when the framework's routes differ from the file scan, discovery: "files" in the named-routes config (creating named-routes.config.mjs when there is none), so the generated module stays the same until you remove the pins. It is a dry run unless you pass --write, and it never edits framework configs or application code. doctor --v2 lists the rest (Node.js, TypeScript, moduleResolution, error codes).

Use npx @triooo/named-routes generate for a standalone invocation or npm exec -- named-routes generate with the package installed. The unscoped named-routes package is unrelated. --base-path /docs overrides the router base for this invocation; --base-path / clears it.

**Base override.** --base-path <path> is supported by generation/check/watch and doctor. It overrides cached framework base and the shared default for that invocation; / clears the base. Framework integration snapshots are generated metadata, not source files.

For a locally installed package, use pnpm exec named-routes list (pnpm) or npm exec --package=@triooo/named-routes -- named-routes list (npm). If Windows reports MODULE_NOT_FOUND before the CLI starts, inspect the generated command shim and reinstall with the original package manager. A shim pointing outside node_modules cannot be repaired by CLI code that never runs. The package bin metadata points to bin/named-routes.js; the launcher loads dist/cli.js relative to itself, preserving the project working directory.

```sh
npx @triooo/named-routes --help
```

Related topic IDs: cli-init, cli-generate, cli-list, cli-check, cli-watch, doctor, audit, cli-migrate
---

# Diagnostics: named-routes doctor

Topic: `doctor` · Named Routes v2.2.0

npx @triooo/named-routes doctor checks the Node.js and TypeScript versions, the configuration file, the detected framework, discovered routes, conflicts and name collisions, whether the generated module exists and is current, the Next.js or Vite integration, typedRoutes without typed hrefs, i18n without localized routes, and route declarations the file scanner cannot see (Nuxt definePageMeta({ path }) and route() calls in a React Router app/routes.ts).

It is read-only: it never writes files and never executes application code. Integration and declaration checks are plain-text heuristics and say so. Options passed inline to a plugin are code, so doctor reports them as not visible; move shared options to named-routes.config.* or pass flags such as --output.

Each diagnostic is error, warning or info, with a stable id and, when known, the file, route, option and a fix. --json prints a machine-readable report for CI and --strict also fails on warnings; colors are used only on a TTY and never with NO_COLOR or --no-color. Exit code 0 means no errors; 1 means errors, or warnings with --strict.

It also says where the routes came from (the framework's table or the files, and why it fell back) and lists the routes that exist in only one of the two views. doctor --v2 adds what a project written for 1.x must change for 2.0: typed hrefs, routes that framework discovery changes, a moduleResolution that cannot read the package's exports, and code that compares error codes with GENERATION_ERROR.

```sh
npx @triooo/named-routes doctor
npx @triooo/named-routes doctor --json --strict   # CI
npx @triooo/named-routes doctor --v2              # upgrading from 1.x

# info     Routes come from the framework: typed-router.d.ts.
# info     /sobre (sobre) exists only in the framework's route table; the file conventions do not produce it.
#          file:  src/pages/about.vue
```
---

# Audit routes and assets

Topic: `audit` · Named Routes v2.2.0

Run audit in the consumer project to detect literal unknown route/asset references, case mismatches, duplicate base prefixes and hardcoded paths. Scans source files, skips build outputs and never rewrites them. This is a conservative lexical audit, not a full language parser: aliases, multiline expressions and dynamic URLs may be missed; hardcoded references and src warnings require review. Errors exit 1; --strict makes warnings fail, and --json gives machine-readable diagnostics.

```sh
npx @triooo/named-routes audit
npx @triooo/named-routes audit --json
npx @triooo/named-routes audit --strict
```
---

```sh
npx @triooo/named-routes migrate --to 2
```

# Discovery edge cases

Topic: `discovery` · Named Routes v2.2.0

Next.js: the scanner considers app and pages together. The root app directory takes precedence over src/app, independently of the same pages/src/pages rule. Other frameworks use their standard folders (Nuxt app/pages or pages, Vue src/pages, SvelteKit src/routes, Astro src/pages, React Router app/routes, TanStack src/routes) unless routesDir is set. Directory symlinks, hidden folders and node_modules are not followed; .d.ts files are ignored.

App Router: only page files are included by default. Groups and slots do not compose URLs. Interceptions are resolved to canonical paths and equivalent variants are consolidated. Private _ folders are ignored; %5F produces a public underscore. Layout, loading, default, error and metadata files are excluded.

Pages Router: root _app, _document and _error are excluded; other underscore pages remain valid. index is removed. API Routes, Route Handlers and other frameworks' endpoints are opt-in through includeApi or --api. URLs do not model HTTP methods, permissions or endpoint validation.

Conflicting URL shapes (for example [id] and [slug] at the same place) and inferred name collisions fail generation. In Next.js, duplicate canonical URLs and optional catch-all specificity conflicts also fail, as they do in Next. In nested-layout routers (Nuxt, Vue, React Router, TanStack), a layout and its index sharing a URL merge into one route.

With framework discovery, the framework's table replaces the page scan; endpoints (includeApi) are still read from their folders, exclude still applies to the reported files, and aliases (Nuxt alias) get their own names. named-routes doctor lists every route that exists in only one of the two views, so you can see what definePageMeta, definePage or routes.ts changed.
---

# Automatic development updates

Topic: `development` · Named Routes v2.2.0

Next.js: the wrapper generates before Next starts, then keeps the module current inside the development process. By default (watchMode: "auto") it reacts to file events from the route directories and the project root, debounced and serialized, plus a rescan every 5 seconds for events the OS dropped. It sees additions, removals and renamed pages; the module changes only when its content changes. No webpack or Turbopack hooks are patched. It never writes during next start (production server), so read-only deployments are safe.

Vite frameworks: the plugin generates in buildStart, once more before the module is first loaded (after the framework has written its route table), and reacts to add/unlink events from Vite's watcher, changes to the named-routes config file and rewrites of typed-router.d.ts, routeTree.gen.ts or app/routes.ts. It finds the project root by walking up from Vite's root to package.json. The Nuxt module regenerates on every pages:resolved, which Nuxt calls when pages change.

Watchers do not run during production builds and do not keep the process alive by themselves. A generation error during editing preserves the last valid module and logs the error. Changes to modules imported by the config need a restart. The config file itself is re-imported only when its content changes; Node.js cannot unload ES modules, so each distinct version of a JavaScript or TypeScript config stays in memory (the config module only, not what it imports) until the process restarts. watch: false disables only ongoing updates, not initial generation.

Where file events are unreliable, polling takes over: WSL paths under /mnt, WATCHPACK_POLLING or CHOKIDAR_USEPOLLING set, NAMED_ROUTES_WATCH=poll, or the OS refusing watchers (for example EMFILE or ENOSPC, reported once). watchMode: "poll" restores the 1.0 behavior (a full rescan every watchInterval). In a reproducible benchmark (pnpm bench:watch, Linux, Node 26) with 200 routes, idle CPU fell from 36 to 6 ms per second and a new page reached the module in 90 ms instead of 478 ms; with 2000 routes, from 153 to 29 ms per second and 203 ms instead of 582 ms.
---

# Errors and troubleshooting

Topic: `errors` · Named Routes v2.2.0

NamedRouteError extends Error and exposes a stable code. UNKNOWN_ROUTE means the name is absent; MISSING_PARAMETER means a required value was omitted; UNKNOWN_PARAMETER means an extra key belongs in query or is misspelled; INVALID_PARAMETER means a value has the wrong shape or contains a forbidden segment; INVALID_LOCALE means a locale was passed without i18n or is not configured.

INVALID_PATTERN, INVALID_NAME and INVALID_MANIFEST identify malformed route definitions. INVALID_OPTIONS, INVALID_QUERY and INVALID_HASH identify invalid options. INVALID_BASE_PATH, INVALID_ORIGIN and INVALID_I18N reject URL defaults. MISSING_ORIGIN requires an origin before requesting absolute URLs. GENERATION_ERROR covers discovery conflicts, routes that cannot be named and stale check results; INVALID_CONFIG covers every invalid option: missing, malformed or misspelled configuration, router, pageExtensions, discovery and output.

Cannot find routes.generated: confirm the integration runs, run generate, and check output/import aliases. Duplicate basePath or locale: use plain relative URLs with framework links and pass basePath/locale only for plain URLs. Stale names: confirm the watcher is enabled and inspect terminal errors. A type error after moving a page is expected: update the inferred name or define a stable override.

Generation refuses to overwrite a handwritten output file. Choose a different output rather than adding a generated signature to unrelated code. Keep generated output outside routable files. Dynamic interpolation does not authorize a request; validate permissions and application input at the destination.

Since 1.1 every NamedRouteError also has details: { file, files, route, pattern, option, hint } with whatever is known, for example both files of a route conflict or "Did you mean users.show?" for a misspelled name, option or names key. INVALID_QUERY means a query failed its schema or a schema map is invalid; INVALID_URL means match() received something that is not a path or URL. Since 2.0 invalid router, pageExtensions and output values raise INVALID_CONFIG (GENERATION_ERROR in 1.x); messages are unchanged.

For static-file 404s, check the actual deployment path and the public directory. `asset()` uses the configured asset base, not the bundler output or the current request. `INVALID_ASSET_BASE`, `INVALID_ASSET` and `INVALID_OPTIONS` identify invalid prefixes, paths and options.

```ts
import { NamedRouteError } from "@triooo/named-routes";
try {
  route("users.$user", { user: "" });
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof NamedRouteError) console.error(error.code);
  else throw error;
}
```
---

# Rewrites and boundaries

Topic: `boundaries` · Named Routes v2.2.0

This is a URL builder, not a replacement router, middleware, authorization system or HTTP client. It does not create routes at runtime, validate resource existence, detect the visitor's locale or make backend requests.

Redirects, rewrites and middleware-based locale detection remain application concerns; paths declared in code are named only where the framework publishes its route table (see Other frameworks). Explicitly map any external or rewritten pattern you need with extraRoutes, and avoid applying locale or basePath twice. The scanner does not read framework config files; use withNamedRoutes or options to pass settings.

```ts
export default defineConfig({
  // A rewrite destination with no page file:
  extraRoutes: { "legacy.post": "/blog/[slug]" },
});
route("legacy.post", { slug: "hello" }); // /blog/hello
```


# AI agents & MCP

# AI agents & MCP

Topic: `ai-agents` · Named Routes v2.2.0

Use llms.txt as the index and llms-full.txt as the versioned reference. Inspect the actual generated manifest and framework settings before writing code. Examples cover root and subpath deployments.

The read-only stdio MCP server is included in @triooo/named-routes. Run pnpm exec named-routes mcp or pnpm exec named-routes-mcp; add --root <project> and optionally --manifest <relative-file> for inventory. Without a root, only documentation is available. Optional dependencies are installed by default; enable them if omitted. No application code is executed or files changed.

Use pnpm run docs, pnpm run test:mcp and pnpm run test:package before releasing the root package. See mcp/README.md for AI clients and Inspector. The catalog version matches the runtime release, but a project manifest may be stale.

Related topic IDs: overview, cli, configuration, public-url, mcp-installation, mcp-project, mcp-tools, mcp-workflow, mcp-security
---

# Install and start MCP

Topic: `mcp-installation` · Named Routes v2.2.0

The Model Context Protocol server is part of @triooo/named-routes. Install the main package only, with optional dependencies enabled. No separate MCP package, web server, API key or account is required.

Use Node.js 22.12 or newer. Run --help and --version to verify the launcher. A bare mcp command starts a stdio server that waits for a client; it is not an HTTP endpoint. Run the commands individually.

The npm and pnpm installation commands are alternatives. Use your existing package manager. After publication, npx can run the package without adding it to the project; pin a version that includes MCP when reproducibility matters.

```sh
pnpm add @triooo/named-routes
# or: npm install @triooo/named-routes

pnpm exec named-routes mcp --help
pnpm exec named-routes-mcp --version

# Start the server (alternative commands):
pnpm exec named-routes mcp
npm exec --package=@triooo/named-routes -- named-routes mcp
npx -y @triooo/named-routes mcp
```

Related topic IDs: mcp-project, mcp-claude, mcp-troubleshooting
---

# Connect a local project

Topic: `mcp-project` · Named Routes v2.2.0

Without --root, the server exposes documentation only. To inspect project routes, configure the trusted project directory explicitly. The server does not discover routes by running the framework. First generate the module in the consumer using its existing integration or CLI.

Use --manifest for custom outputs or if multiple generated modules exist. Its value is relative to --root. Common outputs include src/routes.generated.ts, app/routes.generated.ts and src/lib/routes.generated.ts. In a monorepo point --root at the actual application.

The selected file must be a recognized, static generated TS/JS manifest within the trusted root, under 2 MiB. Route inventory does not verify manifest freshness, HTTP methods, authorization, assets, defaults or deployed pages.

```sh
pnpm exec named-routes generate
# In the MCP client, choose one invocation:
pnpm exec named-routes mcp --root "C:/dev/my-app"
pnpm exec named-routes-mcp --root "C:/dev/my-app" --manifest "src/routes.generated.ts"
```

Related topic IDs: mcp-installation, mcp-tools, mcp-workflow, mcp-troubleshooting
---

# Claude Desktop and Claude Code

Topic: `mcp-claude` · Named Routes v2.2.0

In Claude Desktop, add the server under mcpServers in its local MCP configuration (Developer settings). Merge the entry into your existing JSON; do not replace other servers. Restart the client and inspect available tools.

For Claude Code, use its MCP configuration or claude mcp add --transport stdio named-routes -- npx -y @triooo/named-routes mcp --root C:/dev/my-app. Verify with claude mcp list. Pin the release if necessary. On Windows, the absolute Node launcher shown in the Windows guide avoids npx shim issues.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "named-routes": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "@triooo/named-routes",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "C:/dev/my-app"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Related topic IDs: mcp-project, mcp-windows, mcp-workflow

# Codex configuration
