# Windows and direct Node launcher

Topic: `mcp-windows` · Named Routes v2.2.0

If npx or a .cmd shim fails with MODULE_NOT_FOUND before the CLI starts, resolve the installed package and launch its bin file directly using node. This avoids relying on the package-manager executable shim.

The configuration below uses forward slashes in JSON and an absolute path. With pnpm, symlinks in node_modules normally resolve to the package. If needed, locate package.json with node -p "require.resolve('@triooo/named-routes/package.json')" from the consumer, then use bin/named-routes-mcp.js relative to its directory.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "named-routes": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": [
        "C:/dev/my-app/node_modules/@triooo/named-routes/bin/named-routes-mcp.js",
        "--root",
        "C:/dev/my-app"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Related topic IDs: mcp-installation, mcp-project, mcp-troubleshooting

# Tools and resources

Topic: `mcp-tools` · Named Routes v2.2.0

Use get_agent_contract to read the versioned conventions; search_docs to discover topic IDs; get_topic to read a complete topic; get_framework_guide to list topics for one framework. Documentation queries accept locale en, pt, es or ja.

list_routes filters by name or pattern and paginates using offset and limit (1–100). get_route looks up an exact name. Both require --root. The resource named-routes://agent-contract provides the same agent contract.

The JSON below shows individual tools/call payloads, grouped as an array only for illustration. Call each tool independently through the MCP client; this is not a new batch API.

```json
[
  {
    "name": "get_agent_contract",
    "arguments": {}
  },
  {
    "name": "search_docs",
    "arguments": {
      "query": "Astro base path",
      "locale": "en",
      "limit": 5
    }
  },
  {
    "name": "get_topic",
    "arguments": {
      "id": "astro",
      "locale": "pt"
    }
  },
  {
    "name": "get_framework_guide",
    "arguments": {
      "framework": "astro",
      "locale": "en"
    }
  },
  {
    "name": "list_routes",
    "arguments": {
      "filter": "admin.alunos",
      "offset": 0,
      "limit": 20
    }
  },
  {
    "name": "get_route",
    "arguments": {
      "name": "admin.alunos.edit"
    }
  }
]
```

Related topic IDs: mcp-project, mcp-workflow, mcp-security
---

# Example: build a link from real routes

Topic: `mcp-workflow` · Named Routes v2.2.0

Example prompt: "Read the Named Routes contract and list admin.alunos routes; create a Next.js link for editing a student. Do not invent names or modify the generated manifest." The agent should use get_agent_contract, then list_routes, then get_route if needed.

Assume the returned route is admin.alunos.edit with pattern /admin/alunos/[aluno]/edit. This is illustrative, not a built-in route. If the name or parameter differs, use the actual manifest.

For Next.js Link, route returns the internal URL and Next adds its configured base. For a plain public URL, use route.url. Without a base, the public path is /admin/alunos/42/edit; with base /app it is /app/admin/alunos/42/edit. Validate the generated code with the consumer type checker.

## Without base path

With the app at the domain root, both the internal Next Link and public URL point to the same path.

```tsx
import Link from "next/link";
import { route } from "@/routes.generated";
<Link href={route("admin.alunos.edit", { aluno: 42 })}>Edit</Link>;
route.url("admin.alunos.edit", { params: { aluno: 42 } });
// /admin/alunos/42/edit
```

## With base path

Assuming Next basePath: "/app", keep the native Link internal. route.url includes the prefix for a plain anchor or a shared URL.

```tsx
import Link from "next/link";
import { route } from "@/routes.generated";
<Link href={route("admin.alunos.edit", { aluno: 42 })}>Edit</Link>;
// Next Link adds /app
<a href={route.url("admin.alunos.edit", { params: { aluno: 42 } })}>Edit</a>;
// /app/admin/alunos/42/edit
```

Related topic IDs: mcp-tools, mcp-project, helper-route, base-path
---

# Security and scope

Topic: `mcp-security` · Named Routes v2.2.0

The server is read-only and local over stdio. It parses static generated manifests as data rather than executing them. It does not run shell commands, execute application configuration, write files, call HTTP endpoints or expose a remote service.

Only select a trusted workspace. The manifest is not a sandbox for hostile filesystems. Agents and clients may have additional independent permissions; MCP read-only annotations are not a global security guarantee. Never put credentials in generated defaults or prompts.

Related topic IDs: mcp-project, mcp-tools, ai-agents
---

# Inspector and troubleshooting

Topic: `mcp-troubleshooting` · Named Routes v2.2.0

Use MCP Inspector to inspect tools and their results without a model. Run the installed package launcher from the consumer. The repository maintainer can run pnpm run test:mcp and pnpm run test:package from the root.

Missing optional dependencies: reinstall with optional dependencies enabled, for example npm install --include=optional. With pnpm, remove the no-optional setting and reinstall. A missing or ambiguous manifest requires generation or --manifest. If no routes are available, verify --root. For Windows MODULE_NOT_FOUND use the direct Node launcher.

A stdio server that waits without printing ordinary log output is normal. Protocol messages use stdout; diagnostics use stderr. If documentation differs from the application, compare the installed package version with the catalog version and regenerate routes intentionally before restarting.

```sh
npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector node node_modules/@triooo/named-routes/bin/named-routes-mcp.js --root .
```

Related topic IDs: mcp-windows, mcp-installation, mcp-project, mcp-tools


# Project & releases

# Documentation website

Topic: `website` · Named Routes v2.2.0

This documentation is a Next.js app in website/. It is the project's public site, built with the package itself: every internal link uses route(), the playground and destination pages are real App Router routes, and the English, Portuguese, Spanish and Japanese content comes from the same docs/content.json that renders the README files.

The landing page shows each supported framework as a line on a transit map, a departure board fed with real generator output, a compatibility table and an install journey. Motion is finite or user-driven, pauses off screen, and is disabled by prefers-reduced-motion.

To deploy on Vercel, create a project with Root Directory set to website and keep "Include files outside the root directory" enabled. website/vercel.json installs the repository, builds the package and then builds the site. No environment variables are required.

```sh
# From the repository root:
pnpm install
pnpm build
pnpm --dir website install
pnpm --dir website dev
# http://localhost:3000
pnpm --dir website build
```
---

# Try it: framework demos

Topic: `demos` · Named Routes v2.2.0

examples/ holds a small runnable app per supported setup: app-router and pages-router (Next.js), nuxt, vue (Vue Router 5), sveltekit, astro, react-router (flat routes), tanstack-router and react (routes declared by hand with createRoutes). Each one links to a static page, a dynamic users or posts page and a catch-all docs page by name; the Next.js demos also use typedRoutes with typed hrefs (App Router) and i18n with query strings (Pages Router). pnpm test:e2e installs the packed tarball into a copy of each demo and checks build, production server, browser navigation and live page discovery.

The demos depend on the package through file:../.., so build the package once at the repository root, then install and run any demo with npm. The generated module appears on the first dev or build run and changes as you add pages. Each demo builds with its real framework.

```sh
# Repository root, once:
pnpm install && pnpm build

# Any demo:
cd examples/nuxt        # or vue, sveltekit, astro, react-router, tanstack-router, react
npm install
npm run dev
# create a page and watch routes.generated.ts update
```
---

# Contribute step by step

Topic: `contributing` · Named Routes v2.2.0

**1. Prerequisites.** Install Node.js 22.12 or newer (22.18+ if you want to load named-routes.config.ts files), Git and Python 3 (only used to render the README files). Enable pnpm 12.16.1, the version pinned in package.json: corepack enable, or npm install --global pnpm@12.16.1.

**2. Clone and build.** Clone the repository, run pnpm install at the root and then pnpm build. The build cleans dist/ and compiles src/*.ts to ESM JavaScript, declarations and source maps. Run pnpm build again after every change to src/: the website and the demos use dist/, not the TypeScript sources.

**3. Know the layout.** src/index.ts is the browser-safe runtime (createRoutes, i18n, patterns); src/frameworks.ts holds the file-convention adapters; src/generator.ts discovers, validates and writes the module; src/config.ts loads named-routes.config.*; src/next.ts and src/vite.ts are the integrations; src/cli.ts is the named-routes binary. tests/ has the Node test suite and smoke tests. docs/locales.json lists the languages, docs/content.json holds the multilingual documentation and website/messages/<code>.json the interface texts. website/ is this site, examples/ has one demo per framework and scripts/ has the release, documentation and language helpers.

**4. Test while you work.** pnpm check builds and runs every Node test plus the positive and negative TypeScript contracts; it is what CI runs on Node 20, 22, 24 and 26. pnpm test:next starts real Next.js dev servers (install examples/app-router first with pnpm --dir examples/app-router install). pnpm test:vite starts a real Vite dev server. pnpm test:package packs the tarball and installs it into a clean project. pnpm release:check runs all of them.

**5. Edit the documentation.** docs/content.json is the single source for the website and every README. Each section has an id, title.<code>, paragraphs.<code> (an array of paragraphs per language), code and language; the codes are en, pt, es and ja. English is the source language: write the English text first and keep the same number of paragraphs in every language. **text** renders as bold on the site and in the README. A new section must also be added to a group in docs/groups.json (the website sidebar and the README topic pages), otherwise pnpm run docs fails. Its page is /docs/<id>.

**6. Translate and synchronize the languages.** Run pnpm locales (node scripts/sync-locales.mjs) after changing English text. It compares every language with English in docs/content.json and website/messages/*.json, fills anything missing with the English text so the site keeps working, removes interface keys that no longer exist in English, reorders keys to match en.json and prints a "Needs translation" list. Translate each listed entry in its language, then run pnpm locales:check (node scripts/sync-locales.mjs --check): it changes nothing and fails on missing titles or paragraphs, a different paragraph count, unbalanced **bold** markers, missing or stale interface keys, different ICU placeholders such as {count}, keys out of order or a language missing from website/lib/locales.ts. CI runs this check. node scripts/sync-locales.mjs --untranslated also lists texts that are still identical to English, which helps to review a language before a release.

**7. Sync the README files.** Run pnpm run docs (python3 scripts/sync-docs.py) to regenerate README.md, README.pt-BR.md, README.es.md and README.ja.md (the essentials and an index) and the topic pages in docs/<code>/*.md (one per group of docs/groups.json) from docs/content.json, docs/groups.json and docs/locales.json, then commit all of them. pnpm run docs:check fails when any of these files is out of date; CI runs it, so never edit them by hand. The usual order is: edit English, pnpm locales, translate, pnpm locales:check, pnpm run docs.

**8. Add a new language.** (a) Add an entry to docs/locales.json with code, name, htmlLang, readme (for example README.fr.md) and the README labels contents, references, localGuide, documentation, back, previous and next. (b) Add the code to the Locale union in website/lib/locales.ts and a title for it to every group in docs/groups.json. (c) Run pnpm locales: it creates website/messages/<code>.json and fills docs/content.json with English placeholders. (d) Translate every entry it reports. (e) Add the new README to the files list in package.json. (f) If the script needs other fonts or line breaking (as Japanese does), add rules for html[lang="<code>"] in website/app/transit.css. (g) Run pnpm locales:check, pnpm run docs, pnpm --dir website check:i18n and pnpm --dir website build. The language switcher in the header picks the new language up automatically.

**9. Edit website texts.** Interface strings live in website/messages/<code>.json under ui, with identical keys in every file; ICU syntax is checked, so avoid unescaped braces and keep placeholders identical. Add new keys to en.json first, then run pnpm locales and translate them. pnpm --dir website check:i18n validates every catalog. Framework data shown on the landing page (board rows, map lines, compatibility table) lives in website/lib/transit.ts and must match real generator output.

**10. Run the website.** After pnpm build at the root, run pnpm --dir website install once and pnpm --dir website dev (or pnpm website). The site depends on the package through link:.., so rebuild the package and restart the dev server after changing src/. Switch languages with EN, PT, ES and JA in the header. Before a pull request run pnpm --dir website typecheck and pnpm --dir website build.

**11. Try a demo.** Each folder in examples/ is a small app: cd examples/sveltekit (or nuxt, vue, astro, react-router, tanstack-router, react), npm install, npm run dev. Add a page and watch its routes.generated.ts change. The Next.js demos use pnpm.

**12. Add a framework.** Write the adapter in src/frameworks.ts (sources, extensions, skipDirectory, map) and teach detectFramework its package; add convention tests to tests/frameworks.test.mjs; add a demo to examples/ and the demos workflow matrix; document it in docs/content.json in every language; add its line to website/lib/transit.ts only after the demo builds.

**13. Open a pull request.** Keep the change focused, add regression tests, update CHANGELOG.md under the next version, run pnpm release:check, pnpm locales:check and pnpm run docs:check, and never commit generated files (dist/, routes.generated.ts, .next/, demo build output); .gitignore already excludes them.

**14. Releases (maintainers).** Bump version in package.json, move the CHANGELOG entry under it, run pnpm release:check, then publish a GitHub release tagged named-routes-vX.Y.Z. The publish workflow validates the tag, runs CI again and publishes to npm with provenance through npm trusted publishing (no npm token is stored). Apache License 2.0 applies; bundled fonts keep their OFL licenses.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/trbros/named-routes.git
cd named-routes
pnpm install
pnpm run check
```

Related topic IDs: website, demos, versioning, cli-check
---

# Versions and upgrades

Topic: `versioning` · Named Routes v2.2.0

Version 2.x defines the public contract for inferred names, typed URL generation, framework adapters and framework discovery, i18n, the Next.js wrapper, the Nuxt module, the Vite plugin and the CLI. 1.x receives no new features.

Patch releases preserve the documented API while fixing bugs. Minor releases add compatible functionality, such as new framework adapters. Breaking changes require a new major version. Review the changelog before upgrading.

After an upgrade, restart the dev server to regenerate the manifest and run your application’s type check and navigation tests. If you move a page and need to preserve its public route name, use an explicit alias.

```sh
npm install @triooo/named-routes@^2
npx @triooo/named-routes check
npx tsc --noEmit
```
---

# Upgrading from 1.x

Topic: `migration` · Named Routes v2.2.0

2.0 changes defaults only where the change pays off; every change can be undone in the config. Run npx @triooo/named-routes doctor --v2 to see what applies to your project, then npx @triooo/named-routes migrate --to 2 (dry run) and --write to pin the 1.x behavior where the generated module would change. Remove the pinned lines when you are ready to adopt the new defaults.

Node.js 22.12+ is required (20 is end-of-life since April 2026); it brings require() of ES modules and native recursive file watching everywhere. TypeScript 5.4+ is required for the exported types, the minimum of Zod 4 and Valibot 1 as well.

route() returns typed hrefs by default. Before: string. After: `/users/${string}`, accepted by Next.js typedRoutes without casts. Code that stores a route in a variable and later assigns another string to it fails to compile: annotate it as string, or set hrefs: "string".

Routes come from the framework where it publishes its table (Nuxt module, Vue Router 5, React Router, TanStack Router). Before: definePageMeta/definePage paths and app/routes.ts routes needed extraRoutes. After: they are named like any page, and extraRoutes duplicates of them can be removed. Set discovery: "files" to keep the file scan. In Nuxt, replace the Vite plugin with modules: ["@triooo/named-routes/nuxt"].

Invalid router, pageExtensions and output values raise INVALID_CONFIG instead of GENERATION_ERROR, so each error class has one code; check error.code comparisons. typesVersions was removed: TypeScript must resolve the package through exports, with moduleResolution bundler, node16 or nodenext (node10 cannot). Generated modules that import query schemas as types now use TypeOnlyQueries, so route.parseQuery() is typed as returning the raw query there.

```sh
npx @triooo/named-routes doctor --v2
npx @triooo/named-routes migrate --to 2           # dry run
npx @triooo/named-routes migrate --to 2 --write   # pins hrefs/discovery in named-routes.config

# Keep a reassigned route as a string
const [href, setHref] = useState<string>(route("home"));
```
---

# Helpers playground

Topic: `helpers-playground` · Named Routes v2.2.0

Open /playground and scroll to the URL helpers lab. Change basePath, origin, CDN, locale, path, query and strict/version settings. Results run the real package runtime with illustrative asset metadata. The browser does not scan local files; use the CLI audit in the project.
